_comment: Document intake and accounts-payable control chain (P8b). The customer already has invoices; this block adds no OCR engine, no payment provider and no ERP write. It runs the boring checks that decide whether an invoice should be paid: is it a duplicate, does it agree with the purchase order and the delivery note, did the supplier's bank account change. Copy the 'documents' block below into config/integrations.json, merged under the tenant key next to 'sheets_registers', 'whatsapp' and 'business_graph'.
_note_no_money: The platform does not move money. There is no tool, function or configuration key anywhere in this block that pays, transfers, settles or refunds: the furthest it goes is a posting PLAN, which is a proposal and a 'write', so the engine requires a human approval before it is recorded. PRD v0.5 section 8 puts this in the product's own scope ('it prepares the document and puts the payment up for approval'). The absence is asserted structurally by the test suite and measured by scripts/probe_document_no_payment.py, not merely promised here.
_note_extraction: Extraction is not this block's job. The fields arrive already extracted, either by the model from a document the operator supplied or from the operator's own intake pipeline, and the platform runs the deterministic control chain over them. There is deliberately no PDF or OCR library in the runtime: an extraction quality problem is the extractor's, and quietly guessing at a scanned amount would be worse than refusing it. What this block owns is everything after extraction, and every step of it is reproducible.
_note_money: Money is validated and compared as an INTEGER count of minor units (tiyin for UZS, cents for USD/EUR/RUB). A float is refused outright, because binary floating point cannot hold every decimal amount exactly and an accounts-payable check that is off by one tiyin is a check nobody should trust. An operator writes '1250000.50' as a string or an integer; the platform truncates to the currency's precision rather than rounding, because rounding a submitted amount upward would inflate what it is later compared against.
_note_integrity: A document that disagrees with itself is refused before any check runs: if line items are supplied, their sum must equal the stated total. Otherwise the total compared against the purchase order is a number the document itself contradicts, and a later check built on the wrong total is worse than no check. An ambiguous date such as 10.01.2026 is also refused rather than guessed, because guessing shifts a duplicate window by months.
_note_dedup: The duplicate key is (document kind, supplier, supplier's number) and deliberately excludes the amount. The same invoice number from two different suppliers is two different invoices; the same number from one supplier with a DIFFERENT amount is more suspicious than an exact repeat, not less, so an altered duplicate raises a material fraud signal. A re-submitted number never overwrites the stored original, because the original is the evidence of what was first seen.
_note_match: The three-way match compares the invoice against a purchase order and a delivery note. A missing counterpart yields 'incomplete', a disagreeing one yields 'mismatch': absent evidence and contradicting evidence are different facts and an approver must be able to tell them apart. tolerance_minor is the operator's own allowance, in minor units; with none declared the required agreement is exact, because a non-zero default would silently excuse mismatches the operator never agreed to excuse. Two different currencies are never compared without a rate, because that would invent a number.
_note_fraud: Fraud controls report SIGNALS WITH EVIDENCE and never a verdict. The platform does not accuse, score or block. Each signal names the observation that produced it, because a flag an approver cannot check is a flag an approver will learn to ignore. Signals are split into material ones that hold a posting (an altered duplicate, an outlier amount, a changed bank account) and weak ones that are reported without gating (a round number, a weekend date, no history): most legitimate invoices are round numbers, so gating on that would train an approver to click through the warning. The outlier test is deliberately crude - three times the supplier's own median - and is a prompt to look, not a statistical claim.
_note_approval: document.parse and document.posting_plan are 'write', so the engine requires a human approval for each; document.match, document.duplicates and document.fraud_signals are pure reads. The plan is RECOMPUTED at write time rather than trusted from the step arguments, because an approved step replays its arguments and a caller must not be able to approve a clean plan and submit a dirty one under the same fingerprint.
_note_residency: Document and accounting data are not in the three biometric categories, so under the 2026 amendment they may be stored outside Uzbekistan - but only once one of the three transfer bases applies, and the implementing regulations are not yet in force. Hence residency stays an operator setting (uz | any), exactly as elsewhere in this platform.
